Hi Jared — thanks for the clear questions. Below is a concise, non-legal summary and an attached playbook PDF for procurement. High level answers first, then short technical notes.

1) Deletion scope and cross-cloud artifacts — summary: Redwood enforces logical deletion at the customer-tenancy level and initiates a deletion workflow that covers all persistent stores and cached KV across our serving fleet. For hosted Marketplace listings, we commit to removing customer data from primary and replicated persistent stores within 30 days by default. Transient in-memory caches (KV caches on serving nodes) are purged on a rolling schedule and we treat purge + TTL enforcement as part of the 30-day window; we also perform a targeted cache flush for deletion requests to accelerate removal.

Technical note: we do not replicate persistent customer blobs to other cloud providers for the same tenancy unless configured for cross-cloud disaster recovery; we may spill inference state (short-lived KV/cache entries) to nearest-region serving nodes — those are ephemeral and evicted within minutes to hours. We include a cache invalidation step in the deletion playbook that triggers via orchestration to ensure no serving node retains a valid reference to deleted keys.

2) Policy precedence between Marketplace and customer-managed onboarding YAML — summary: precedence is: customer-managed retention (explicit in onboarding YAML) can only relax retention downward (shorten retention) if it does not violate Marketplace minimums or contractual obligations. The Marketplace listing sets a floor (minimum retention) and Redwood enforces that floor; if a customer requests shorter retention than the Marketplace floor we flag the discrepancy and require a contractual amendment.

Technical note: retention settings are applied at two layers — control plane metadata (contract/listing-level defaults) and tenancy-level runtime policies (onboarding YAML). At runtime, the enforcement engine reconciles by computing an effective TTL = max(marketplace_min_ttl, onboarding_requested_ttl). Deletion workflows then honor the effective TTL.
